cards.explanation: The answer is the words from the large scroll. The LORD tells Isaiah, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.” Those are the same words He told Isaiah to write on the scroll back in verse 1. So the name on the scroll is the name for the boy.

The word is carried off. The wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria. And the timing is the wild part, friends: it all happens before the boy can say 'Father' or 'Mother.' I'd say that's a tight deadline.

The answer is True, and it's a sad pairing. The LORD says this people rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah. Rezin is the king of Aram, and the son of Remaliah is Pekah, king of Israel (Isaiah 7:1). They turned down the gentle waters and cheered for those two instead.

The answer is the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates. The Lord says He will surely bring them against this people. The people turned down the gentle waters, and now the waters get anything but gentle. Same theme of water, with a very different size.

The answer is True, because the flood is a picture. The Lord says the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates are "…the king of Assyria and all his pomp." So when the river overflows, think of a king and all his splendor coming across the land. The LORD hands us the meaning Himself.

The answer is Judah. The flood "…will pour into Judah, swirling and sweeping over it, reaching up to the neck…" Judah is the land where Ahaz is king (Isaiah 7:1). The streams spread until they cover the entire land.
The answer is shattered. The message says, "prepare for battle, and be shattered; prepare for battle, and be shattered!" Huddling together and preparing for battle both end in the same word, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; state a proposal, but it will not happen." People can plan all they want, but the plan is thwarted and the proposal doesn't happen. Not one clipboard in the land can change that.

The reason is "For God is with us." It's the last line of the passage. The plans fall apart because God is with His people, not because anyone else got clever. It's a good note to end on after all that flooding and shattering, bakers.
